explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1090 with the answer yes. For each k ≥ 3 there is a finite planar A such that every 2-colouring has a set S ⊆ A of at least k collinear points that equals A ∩ (line through S), checked via affineSpan, and is monochromatic. Since |S| ≥ 3 and S is collinear, affineSpan(S) is exactly a line, so S is all of A's points on that line, as required. Using Fin 2 → ℝ rather than EuclideanSpace is harmless here, because only affine notions are involved.
